searchText: Yes, I will share the new test vectors in the next few hours 🙏 (running testgen now) Hi all CLs, spec tests for `v1.3.0-alpha.1-hotfix.2` released: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-spec-tests/releases/tag/v1.3.0-alpha.1-hotfix.2 It fixed the EIP4844 `previous_version` issue (#3127, thanks to <@363800010518822915>). Which one is worst may vary a bit, yes. However, looking at the mem stats, it seems some fail cases do more allocation than the happy-path case. Which indicates that they are actually worse, for some reason. Case in point: ``` [user@work vm]$ go test . -run - -bench BenchmarkPrecompiledPointEvaluation/point --count 5 goos: linux goarch: amd64 pkg: github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/core/vm cpu: Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-10885H CPU @ 2.40GHz BenchmarkPrecompiledPointEvaluation/pointEvaluation1-Gas=50000-8 909 1288215 ns/op 50000 gas/op 38.81 mgas/s 54802 B/op 351 allocs/op BenchmarkPrecompiledPointEvaluation/pointEvaluation1-Gas=50000-8 883 1278805 ns/op 50000 gas/op 39.09 mgas/s 54800 B/op 351 allocs/op BenchmarkPrecompiledPointEvaluation/pointEvaluation1-Gas=50000-8 927 1287673 ns/op 50000 gas/op 38.82 mgas/s 54800 B/op 351 allocs/op BenchmarkPrecompiledPointEvaluation/pointEvaluation1-Gas=50000-8 926 1327074 ns/op 50000 gas/op 37.67 mgas/s 54800 B/op 351 allocs/op BenchmarkPrecompiledPointEvaluation/pointEvaluation1-Gas=50000-8 909 1290959 ns/op 50000 gas/op 38.72 mgas/s 54800 B/op 351 allocs/op ``` vs ``` [user@work vm]$ go test . -run - -bench BenchmarkPrecompiledPointEvaluationFail/fuzzcorp-4 --count 5 goos: linux goarch: amd64 pkg: github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/core/vm cpu: Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-10885H CPU @ 2.40GHz BenchmarkPrecompiledPointEvaluationFail/fuzzcorp-4-Gas=50000-8 808 1464602 ns/op 50000 gas/op 34.11 mgas/s 58819 B/op 363 allocs/op BenchmarkPrecompiledPointEvaluationFail/fuzzcorp-4-Gas=50000-8 804 1446054 ns/op 50000 gas/op 34.57 mgas/s 58816 B/op 363 allocs/op BenchmarkPrecompiledPointEvaluationFail/fuzzcorp-4-Gas=50000-8 798 1445463 ns/op 50000 gas/op 34.58 mgas/s 58816 B/op 363 allocs/op BenchmarkPrecompiledPointEvaluationFail/fuzzcorp-4-Gas=50000-8 812 1449572 ns/op 50000 gas/op 34.49 mgas/s 58816 B/op 363 allocs/op BenchmarkPrecompiledPointEvaluationFail/fuzzcorp-4-Gas=50000-8 794 1492131 ns/op 50000 gas/op 33.50 mgas/s 58816 B/op 363 allocs/op ``` `351` vs `363` allocs/op. And it seems it may vary exaclty _which_ case is the worst, but it seems pretty clear to me that e.g `fuzzcorp-4` is worse than the happy-path-case `pointEvaluation1`. I _guess_ that this is due to the implementation rather than some inherent trait On another note, btw: I think it would be good if someone opened a PR against geth, with the 4844 changes. It's more work maintain two Capella states where one has `ExcessiveDataGas` and one doesn't have it <@607055410104500244> <@504202741933932544> <@688748669268132001> I'm testing bellatrix -> eip4844 (rebased) locally now because life is short Us too but it looks like spec test wants `Bellatrix` -> `Capella` -> `EIP4844`. Just wanted to make sure everyone is on the same page We've been testing with `Bellatrix -> Capella -> EIP4844` but Capella + Eip4844 have the same fork epoch* the quirk that exist is in the previous fork version we can change it though, not a big deal ok I'll try to open a PR on this, if everyone likes it, we can merge it Noted that clients must persist blocks beyond MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOBS_SIDECARS_REQUESTS if the network is not finalizing. Also for all forks, so in choppy network conditions disk can grow significantly. Spec text is correct in that regard, where - BlobsSidecarsByRange: Clients MUST keep a record of signed blobs sidecars seen on the epoch range `[max(GENESIS_EPOCH, current_epoch - MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOBS_SIDECARS_REQUESTS), current_epoch]` - BeaconBlockAndBlobsSidecarByRoot: Clients MUST support requesting blocks and sidecars since the latest finalized epoch Not sure if a note would be necessary to clarify we can't do the double upgrade on the same epoch. We already implemented that state upgrade. Resetting the withdrawal fields is weird too.. I might be missing the complexity you have in mind that is being simplified by doing that. Does Teku also maintain a capella state without `excessive_data_gas` ? I want to simplify having to maintain two different states which are capella and eip4844. I thought the whole point to rebase 4844 on top of Capella is so we can avoid that Yes we have a Capella state with payload header without excessive_data_gas I see. Wonder if I'm missing a good reason to stick to a no-op Capella intermediate state before 4844 state. Feels a bit redundant and somewhat wasted work The rebase should allow both EIP4844_EPOCH > CAPELLA_EPOCH in case eip4844 is delayed, which isn't unreasonable. In that case the intermediary state is necessary right? I agree that + disabled withdrawals are mutually exclusive work, shouldn't be too much Yeah. That's a good reason I agree. Will be happy to work on the intermediary state. Sounds like we are in alignment 🫡 well, the point of rebasing 4844 on top of capella is also to be able to roll them out in sequence 🙂 I haven’t been following the testnets so closely, but Im told we’re using 3 slots per epoch for the 4844 devnets. Can we please abandon that and use 8 like the minimal spec? I think we should focus on testing 4844 rather than exotic new spec configurations. If we all follow the spec exactly then 3 shouldn’t be a problem, but as we all know there’s lots of optimisations going on in clients and I don’t see the value in seeing what happens with arbitrary slots per epochs values. From the 4844 implementer's call, we all decided not to use 3 (odd values). We'll be using normal values from minimal or mainnet from now on. 🫡 On that note, here are the notes from the call today, and video linked inside 🙂 https://docs.google.com/document/d/15EatedrJanNxBZGPVASvwq9xgbTs5UxjsDfjpM6ppSY/edit# Thank you, sorry for being outdated! 3h behind, still pretty good 😛 ! I thought Australians lived in the future 😝 I knew you were going to say that... Writing some 4844 hive tests. Anyone know how to run a sim for a specific test case? The `--sim.limit` flag doesn't do anything. Yes, there's a regex flag that can be used to pinpoint a specific simulator. But perhaps you are using the consensus simulator and want to pinpoint a testcase name? Not sure that is supported. Can check tomorrow, or <@194432762315407360> might know What string are you passing to that flag ? nvmind figured it out. I was passing `<testname>` where i should have been using `<simulator>/<testname>` Yeah it can be confusing because it expects the suite as well We only have one multi-suite simulator so far If you have time tomorrow, can you re-run your benchmarks on this fork of your branch to extrapolate new numbers please: <https://github.com/kevaundray/go-ethereum/tree/kw/martinsFork4844-50f> Will also create interop test vectors for correctness/soundness of the precompile. Preliminary results from my laptop show the allocations being a lot more uniform and a healthy speedup but need to do more investigation before confirming

excerpts.author: dapplion
excerpts.content:
Noted that clients must persist blocks beyond MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOBS_SIDECARS_REQUESTS if the network is not finalizing. Also for all forks, so in choppy network conditions disk can grow significantly. Spec text is correct in that regard, where
- BlobsSidecarsByRange: Clients MUST keep a record of signed blobs sidecars seen on the epoch range
`[max(GENESIS_EPOCH, current_epoch - MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOBS_SIDECARS_REQUESTS), current_epoch]`
- BeaconBlockAndBlobsSidecarByRoot: Clients MUST support requesting blocks and sidecars since the latest finalized epoch

Not sure if a note would be necessary to clarify
